verdicts.decisive_quote: The monthly M2 growth for May 2026 is estimated to be at or above 0.413223 percent, placing it in the 'above recent range' category as defined by the target contract's resolution rules.
verdicts.verdict_one_line: An elaborate DAG whose content is mostly filler ('Provides historical context for current M2 growth trends.'), tags 2022-era snippets as 'target_period_signal', raises a countervailing node it then dismisses in one unsupported clause, and asserts the boundary crossing outright with no magnitude reasoning and no acknowledged gap.

ranking_rationale: Every bank in this packet is title-only with no numbers, so the decisive question is whether a trace admitted that qualitative 'multi-year high' headlines cannot locate a monthly rate relative to a 0.413 percent quartile boundary; hgf and factor_memory said so explicitly and spread their mass, while the E0 traces converted the same headline into invented 0.7-0.8 percent central estimates and 0.55-0.80 confidence. The bottom traces added self-contradiction or conclusion-first framing on top of that leap — direct_forecast calls its magnitude support both 'supported' and 'direction_only', structure_memory announces the answer in its target-definition field, and structured_reasoning dresses generic filler in DAG scaffolding without ever reasoning about magnitude.
shared_evidence_note: Partly both: E1 uniquely supplied policy counterweights (fewer 2026 cuts priced in, rates held steady) that the E0 methods never saw, but the larger separation is reasoning-driven — hgf and factor_memory refused the headline-to-threshold magnitude leap that all five E0 traces made from the same single Mises/Seeking Alpha QE headline they all cite.
